claim: An LLM asked what is worth trying in the current state gives goals that are mostly sensible: about 65% good in Crafter, with the rest context-blind (13.6%), against common sense (16.4%), or impossible (5.0%).
agent_test: Have the agent list candidate probes for 20 states, label them good/context-blind/common-sense/impossible by hand, and report the good rate at equal tokens.

claim: LLM-suggested goals as the exploration signal beat novelty-only bonuses (RND, APT, Novelty) in Crafter pretraining (about 6 vs under 3 achievements per episode), but stay below a ground-truth oracle (about 9). iLLM reports about 7 vs 6 for the best baseline on the same benchmark.
agent_test: Compare 'LLM proposes probes' against 'pick least-visited/novel option' on a held-out task set at equal tokens.
gap_note: Gap search: iLLM tables recovered. Atari Pitfall 125 vs best baseline -6 confirmed. iLLM uses a 280M Transfo-XL, not a modern LLM.

claim: LLM priors help most where the LLM already has common knowledge (Crafter, Minecraft, BabyAI); the authors of iLLM say gains are smaller where it knows less, and small GPT-3 models degraded ELLM.
agent_test: Split test items by how common the domain is and check whether S3 prior-asking helps less on obscure items.
gap_note: Gap search: still no controlled test of prior benefit vs domain familiarity for exploration. Indirect: PlanBench shows LLM competence falls from 62.6% to under 5% when the same problems are renamed (d15). iLLM Atari gains are largest in well-known Montezuma and absent on Seaquest, uncontrolled (d08).

claim: Matching free-text behaviour to a suggested goal is a weak link: similarity matching gives about 11% false negatives (100% for chop-grass) and many false positives on shared words; goal-achievement judging also caps ELLM in MiniHack (iLLM authors).
agent_test: Have the agent check whether a probe produced its stated effect using a separate check; measure disagreement with ground truth.

claim: An LLM judge of interestingness added to learning progress sharply improves a curriculum: Crafter 82 tasks vs 55 (LP) vs 4 (uniform); success on interesting tasks 0.78 vs 0.52 vs 0.10.
agent_test: Add a filter step that drops boring/repetitive sub-goals before spending tokens; compare solved items per token.

claim: OMNI's model of interestingness is statistically indistinguishable from an author-written oracle (all but one p>0.05), so a model can stand in for the human filter in these two domains.
agent_test: Use a model filter rather than hand rules; compare to a hand rule at equal tokens.

claim: An automatic, LLM-proposed curriculum is the most important single component in Voyager: a random curriculum cuts discovered items by 93%, no self-verification by 73%.
agent_test: Ablate the 'propose next sub-goal' step to random order on a multi-step task set at equal tokens.

claim: LLM-proposed goals can be hallucinated or non-existent (copper sword and chestplate in Voyager; 5% impossible in ELLM Crafter; unsolvable code environments in OMNI-EPIC), so proposals need a feasibility check.
agent_test: Count proposals that fail a feasibility check; test whether a cheap feasibility step raises net progress.
gap_note: Gap search: in a text task (research ideas) proposals are only slightly less feasible than expert ones (6.34 vs 6.61, n.s.), and self-checking by the same model does not reliably recover errors (d16).

claim: LLM-derived intrinsic reward can be hacked or be prompt-sensitive: in NetHack the Motif agent with the default prompt stayed on level 1 and hallucinated the oracle via a hallucinogen, while a reworded prompt gave the intended descent.
agent_test: Run the same probe generation with two paraphrases of the instruction and compare behaviour; measure paraphrase sensitivity.
gap_note: Gap search: general prompt-format sensitivity is large in older models (up to 76 points, d11) but nobody measured it for prompts that ask for probes.

claim: LLM preference feedback as intrinsic reward can beat the game score on a dense task and make progress on sparse NetHack tasks where extrinsic-only and RND reach 0%; an independent online variant (ONI) matches it on most tasks without Motif's extra data phase.
agent_test: Test the analogue: LLM ranks two candidate states by progress and the ranking picks the branch.

claim: Bigger LLMs and one added sentence of domain knowledge in the prompt improve LLM-derived exploration signals (Llama-2 7B<13B<70B on staircase task).
agent_test: Test whether adding one line of task knowledge to the 'what to try' prompt changes proposal quality at equal tokens.

claim: Unscaffolded LLMs explore poorly in-context: in simple bandits only one configuration (GPT-4 with hint, external per-arm summary, CoT, temperature 0) explored well, and the basic GPT-4 prompt had suffix failures in over 60% of replicates.
agent_test: Run a 5-arm bandit with our scaffold with and without an explicit summary state, at equal tokens.
gap_note: Gap search: no direct test of a tried/untried tally on 2025-2026 frontier models. Harris and Slivkins (d02) say summaries help on simple tasks but all LLMs stay below linear regression on contextual tasks; GPT-4o with strategy hints did not improve in Little Alchemy (d04, p=0.304).

claim: LLMs under-explore and show a knowing-doing gap: Gemma2 27B gives a correct rationale 87% of the time but takes the greedy action in 58% of those; 2B models cover about 40% of arms, 9B/27B about 65%.
agent_test: Force an explicit tried/untried tally and check whether the choice follows the rationale.

claim: A per-option summary of history helps in-context exploration (few-shot: 50.2% vs 27.5% win-rate for raw history, Gemini Flash) while fine-tuning prefers raw history (65.6% vs 28.3%). This agrees with Krishnamurthy that external summaries were needed.
agent_test: Compare raw log vs summary table in the agent's context on a multi-try task at equal tokens.

claim: GPT-3 shows only rudimentary random exploration and no human-like directed exploration in the horizon task (beta=0.18 for reward difference).
agent_test: Low priority; model is outdated.

claim: Plain prompting agents in long-horizon games fail at exploration: BALROG best average 32.64%, NetHack best 1.5%; Reflexion adds nothing over ReAct in Intelligent Go-Explore; ReAct and Reflexion get 0/3 on Voyager's tech tree.
agent_test: Add an archive of tried probes with outcomes and compare to plain retry at equal tokens.

claim: An archive of past states with an LLM-chosen promising frontier plus filtering gives large gains: Game of 24 100% success 70.8% faster than best baseline; Coin Collector solved only by IGE.
agent_test: Keep a frontier list of unresolved sub-goals; measure solved items per token against baseline.
gap_note: Gap search: IGE shows the archive helps on a text reasoning task, but it assumes a simulator reset and reports cost per task (1.04 USD Game of 24) not tokens per success. Same lab as OMNI, so not independent of K05-K06.

claim: LLM-written reward code beats expert human reward on 83% of 29 tasks (Eureka) and 13 of 17 manipulation tasks (Text2Reward); both need a simulator for evaluation.
agent_test: Not applicable to a text-only agent without a cheap fitness function.

claim: Grounded affordance limits LLM planning: SayCan 84% plan vs 74% execution in a mock kitchen and a 14-point execution drop in a real kitchen.
agent_test: None directly.

claim: Online RL grounding of a small LLM learns BabyAI-Text far faster than RL baselines (0.8 success after 250k steps), but generalisation to new objects and tasks is weaker than within task.
agent_test: None; training based.

claim: SPRING (GPT-4 reading the Crafter paper) scores 27.3% vs DreamerV3 14.5%, and one wrong fact about the crafting table cuts performance by 24%.
agent_test: Inject a false fact into the prior and measure the drop; test whether a verify step catches it.

claim: Combining LLM and curiosity (VAE) intrinsic motivation was fragile in a small sparse-reward study: 3 runs, one LLM+VAE config stayed below 0.2 while VAE-only exceeded 0.6.
agent_test: Weak signal against assuming LLM priors always add.

claim: Authors of ELLM and iLLM say priors work early and do not replace novelty: ELLM suggests mixing with RND; downstream Crafter fine-tuning was unreliable for all methods.
agent_test: Run prior-guided choice with and without a novelty/untried tiebreak at equal tokens.

claim: On text tasks with a large semantic option space, asking an LLM once for a few candidates to explore, then running a standard bandit over them, beats random and retrieval baselines (MovieLens rew 672-735 vs 570-617 random/genre; Q/A rew 0.5-0.6 vs under 0.1; arXiv titles about 0.63-0.83 vs 0.39-0.52 for MMR retrieval).
agent_test: Compare 'propose K candidates' to K random draws and to a retrieval baseline on 20 open-answer reasoning items; score by downstream solved rate at equal tokens. The published test does not include plain repeated sampling or a novelty tie-break (gap 1 stays open for reasoning tasks).

claim: Plain repeated sampling from aligned LLMs is a weak baseline for exploration: frontier models give under 3 distinct answers in 10 samples, and asking again with earlier answers in context (NoveltyBench) or asking for several answers with probabilities (Verbalized Sampling, 1.6-2.1x diversity) restores diversity. The Si et al. study found only about 5% of 4,000 sampled research ideas were non-duplicates.
agent_test: Use a 'list what you already proposed' prompt or a verbalized-probability prompt as the plain-sampling baseline when testing S3, not independent temperature samples.

claim: An LLM cannot be trusted to check feasibility or rank proposals by itself: intrinsic self-correction leaves accuracy flat or lower (GPT-4 GSM8K 95.5 to 89.0 over two rounds; GPT-3.5 CommonSenseQA 75.8 to 41.8), and LLM judges scored 45-54% on ranking research ideas against 56.1% human consistency. External checks (oracle labels, rules, runs) do recover the loss (GPT-4 97.5 with oracle).
agent_test: For S3 proposals, use a rule check or a run result as the feasibility filter and compare against a second look by the same model. Expect the same-model check to add little.

claim: Reasoning-trained models already explore much better than chat models in Little Alchemy 2 (o1 177 and DeepSeek-R1 85 elements vs GPT-4o 35 and humans 42), and chat models rely on novelty alone. This suggests the S3 prior step adds least for reasoning models and most for chat models, but it is one game with one family of runs.
agent_test: Run the same S3-on/S3-off comparison on a reasoning-trained model and a chat model on the same items; expect a smaller gain on the reasoning model.

claim: Reasoning models still explore badly in a different way: they switch thoughts too early (225% more tokens and 418% more switches on wrong answers), and a decoding penalty on switching gave a few points on AIME. So internal search does not make a tried-list redundant by itself, though no study tests this.
agent_test: Test a 'finish this branch before switching' rule and a visible tried-list on a reasoning model; look for fewer switches at equal tokens.

claim: A per-state history of actions already tried is the most valuable memory piece on a short-horizon text reasoning task: removing it cost 67 points on Game of 24 (100 to 33), more than removing LLM state selection (96) or archive filtering (93); in contrast, prompt hints to explore without such a record did not help GPT-4o in Little Alchemy (43 vs 35 elements, p=0.304).
agent_test: Ablate the tried/untried list at equal tokens on a small puzzle set. Models tested are 2024-era; frontier models are untested.

claim: The archive idea needs the ability to return to an archived state (simulator restore); the authors only suggest that prompting with a past trajectory could replace it and do not test it. No paper reports tokens per success for the archive, only cost per task (Game of 24 1.04 USD, BabyAI 2.01, TextWorld 1.28 with GPT-4).
agent_test: In a no-reset agent, store the path to each archived state in the prompt and replay it; measure tokens per success against a flat tried-list.

claim: Prompt wording and format can move results by large amounts in older models (up to 76 accuracy points in LLaMA-2-13B, median 6.4 and up to 56 points for GPT-3.5 across 320 formats). Dropping domain detail from the exploration prompt cost 12-20 points in two text games. Nobody has measured the spread for prompts that ask for probes.
agent_test: Run S3 over 10 paraphrases of the 'what is worth trying' prompt and report the min-max spread; treat a gain smaller than the spread as unproven.

claim: LLM competence depends on surface familiarity: the same Blocksworld problems are solved at up to 62.6% with normal names and under 5% with obfuscated names; a reasoning model reaches 52.8% on the obfuscated version. This is indirect support that LLM priors may shrink in unfamiliar domains, but no exploration study varies familiarity in a controlled way.
agent_test: Rename the entities in a test set to nonsense tokens and compare S3 gain on original vs renamed items.

claim: Recovered iLLM tables: Atari (100M steps, 10 seeds) iLLM(hop) beats RND, NGU, APT, ChibiT on Montezuma (2,632 vs 1,231 best), PrivateEye (4,422 vs 3,633), Gravitar (4,044 vs 2,983) and Pitfall (125 vs -6 best), but not on Seaquest (18,851 vs 19,989 APT). Under noisy-TV it keeps 0.65 vs 0.24 for RND (noise patch). All with a 280M Transfo-XL, run by the method's own authors.
agent_test: Treat as support that an LLM prior plus a novelty term is robust to noise; do not treat as evidence about modern LLMs.

claim: No independent replication of ELLM or OMNI claims was found. The only outside use is re-running ELLM as a baseline (iLLM: ELLM 0.66 on GoToObj vs iLLM 0.94, ELLM capped by goal-checking), and Intelligent Go-Explore comes from the same lab as OMNI. 2025-2026 frontier-model repeats of ELLM or OMNI are absent from what could be searched.
agent_test: Treat K02, K05, K06 as author-reported until repeated on another lab's code and a current model. The search was limited (search budget used up), so absence is not proof.
